text:
sophia: I moved my desk to the terrace for the day 73314bb posted a pic: https://files.slack.com/archives/random/FZXY1234/IMG_20260402.jpg. Love the light but my laptop keeps dropping Zoom calls. Any quick outdoor-WFH wifi tips?

nate: Nice setup. First try: move the router closer to the terrace or put it on a window sill facing that side. Height matters.

jisoo: If you have a phone with decent LTE, use it as a hotspot during the call. Cheap and fast for a one-off.

sophia: Hotspot is my fallback but I'm mid-demo in 15m so need something that doesn't die.

sam: Can you plug an ethernet into the house jack? If not, get a USB3-to-Ethernet dongle and run an outdoor extension for short-term.

leo: Also check if your laptop is switching between 2.4/5GHz. Force 5GHz and a less crowded channel. On mac: hold Option + click Wi-Fi icon to see channel.

sophia: Is there an easy way to do channel scan? I50e

jisoo: Try WiFi Analyzer on mobile to see congested channels. Or `nmcli device wifi list` on Linux for quick view.

infra-bot: Tip drop: "If you need very short-term stability, tether to your phone and plug the phone into a small power bank; disable Wi-Fi on the phone to force LTE only if in a noisy wifi area." :robot_face:

sophia: Rebooted router, moved it to the sill, set laptop to 5GHz 44d on my next call it felt stable. Will keep the hotspot as backup. Thanks!

nate: If you make it permanent, consider a weatherproof outdoor AP or a directional antenna aimed at the terrace. Overkill for a day but great for recurring outdoor work.

sam: Also pro tip: throw a lightweight blanket over the back of your chair to reduce mic echo if wind picks up.

sophia: Will test mic and post a follow-up pic if the cat approves. :cat:
